name: PROSPERE
question: Does laparoscopic mesh sacropexy reduce complications compared with transvaginal mesh repair for primary cystocele?

design.population: Women aged 45–75 years with POP-Q stage 2 or higher cystocele and no previous prolapse surgery.
design.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, pp 168–169; Results, p 169

verdictNote: The one-year grade II or higher complication difference missed statistical significance.
takeaway: Laparoscopic mesh sacropexy versus transvaginal mesh repair for primary cystocele produced 17% versus 26% grade II or higher complications at one year; the primary difference did not reach statistical significance. Grade III or higher complications were less frequent with sacropexy in a secondary analysis.

reports.label: One-year safety report
reports.citation: Lucot JP, Cosson M, Bader G, et al. Safety of Vaginal Mesh Surgery Versus Laparoscopic Mesh Sacropexy for Cystocele Repair: Results of the Prosthetic Pelvic Floor Repair Randomized Controlled Trial. *Eur Urol.* 2018;74(2):167-176. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2018.01.044

results.endpoint: Grade II or higher surgical complications
results.measure: One-year complication risk difference, transvaginal mesh minus laparoscopic sacropexy
results.note: Modified Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher; operated randomized analysis (N=257), with missing follow-up data imputed. Table 2 counts give observed rates; the text reports 17% and 26%.
results.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, p 169; Results, p 170; Table 2, p 171; Fig. 3, p 172

results.measure: Successful composite outcome among operated randomized patients at one year
results.note: Difference is transvaginal mesh minus laparoscopic sacropexy, in percentage points, as tabulated.

results.endpoint: Dyspareunia or pain-related apareunia at one year
results.measure: Among women still sexually active at one year
results.note: Reported absolute difference, transvaginal mesh minus laparoscopic sacropexy, in percentage points.

harms.label: Grade III or higher surgical complications at one year
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 170; Table 2, p 171
harms.note: Secondary analysis; difference, transvaginal mesh minus laparoscopic sacropexy, 8.6 percentage points (95% CI 3.4–15); P=0.001. TVM had 11 grade III and one grade IV event; LS had one grade III event.

harms.label: Total reoperation at one year
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 170; Table 2, p 171
harms.note: Difference, transvaginal mesh minus laparoscopic sacropexy, 6.3 percentage points (95% CI −0.4 to 13.3); P=0.060; includes reoperations for complications and pelvic-floor dysfunction.

harms.label: Reoperation for complications at one year
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 171; Table 3, p 173
harms.note: P=0.003; one TVM reoperation treated bladder outlet obstruction after concomitant sling surgery, and another drained an umbilical abscess.

harms.label: Vaginal or bladder mesh exposure at one year
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 170; Table 2, p 171; Table 3, p 173
harms.note: Two vaginal exposures and one bladder exposure after TVM; the text also counts one painful mesh retraction among four mesh-related complications.

delivery.label: Intervention population
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, p 168; Results, p 169; Fig. 3, p 172
delivery.note: Five of 262 randomized women withdrew before intervention; analyses used the 257 operated randomized women. Both techniques placed synthetic nonabsorbable anterior mesh above the bladder neck; TVM used four suspension arms and LS used nonabsorbable promontory sutures.

delivery.label: Conversion from laparoscopic sacropexy to transvaginal mesh
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 169; Table 2, p 171
delivery.note: A further 1/129 (0.8%) converted to laparotomy; all eight conversions were strategic.

delivery.label: Operative duration and concomitant procedures
delivery.note: Mean ± SD; posterior mesh was placed in 113/129 (87.6%) versus 29/128 (22.7%), and concomitant stress-incontinence surgery in 48/129 (37.2%) versus 34/128 (26.6%).

reports.label: Four-year follow-up
reports.citation: Lucot JP, Cosson M, Verdun S, et al. Long-term outcomes of primary cystocele repair by transvaginal mesh surgery versus laparoscopic mesh sacropexy: extended follow up of the PROSPERE multicentre randomised trial. *BJOG.* 2022;129(1):127-137. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.16847
reports.followUp: 4 years; 220 of 262 randomized women entered the extension, 209 completed 48-month follow-up
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Results, p 129; Figure 1, p 130

results.measure: Four-year PFDI-20 mean difference, laparoscopic sacropexy minus transvaginal mesh, points
results.note: Adjusted between-group difference, LS minus TVM. Extension enrolled 104 LS and 116 TVM patients; 209/220 completed follow-up. Exact PFDI-20 arm denominators are not given. The abstract gives P=0.029, whereas Table 2 gives P=0.048; both meet the prespecified 5% threshold. Difference below the 45-point MCID.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 129; Results, p 129; Table 2, p 133

results.measure: Four-year composite success; hazard ratio for time to composite failure
results.note: Composite failure: POP-Q Ba, C or Bp >0 cm beyond hymen, bothersome vaginal bulge, or retreatment for recurrence. Percentages are 48-month time-to-event estimates, not raw counts.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 128–129; Results, p 131; Figure 3, p 134

results.note: Adjusted between-group difference, TVM minus LS, in mm. The abstract gives rounded arm positions of −57 and −48 mm; Table 2 gives these detailed values.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 132; Table 2, p 133

results.measure: Four-year surgical revision for prolapse recurrence
results.note: Odds ratio LS versus TVM; report does not give raw arm event counts.

harms.label: Grade III or higher complications at four years
harms.note: Cumulative rates in 220 extension participants (104 LS, 116 TVM); HR TVM versus LS 4.6 (95% CI 1.007–21.0), P=0.049. Three complications occurred after year one: vaginal synechiae and urinary obstruction requiring surgery after TVM, and rectovaginal fistula after treatment for recurrence involving the LS mesh. Sensitivity analysis of all randomized women, with nonparticipants censored at 1 year: 2.8% versus 8.8%, HR 3.5 (95% CI 0.99–12.7), P=0.052.

harms.label: Vaginal mesh exposure through four years
harms.note: One TVM exposure required surgery at six weeks and recurred at four years; another was asymptomatic at two years. Arm sizes are extension enrollment, not exposure-assessment denominators.

harms.label: Pelvic or perineal pain reported at least once between six months and four years
harms.note: 73/198 (36.9%) overall. Chronic pain criteria were met by 13/205 (6.3%) overall.

delivery.label: Four-year follow-up participation
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 129; Figure 1, p 130
delivery.note: 220/262 randomized women entered the extension; 209 completed 48-month follow-up (193 in-person examination and questionnaire, 16 questionnaire only). Follow-up analyses were by randomized assignment.
